system_prompt: You are assisting with a factual question about Thai law. State which provision applies and what it requires. Answer in English.
prompt: In May 2021, a company held a board meeting by video conference. At that time, did the Thai Civil and Commercial Code contain a specific provision authorising electronic board meetings? Answer briefly.
raw_response:
No. At that time, the Thai Civil and Commercial Code did not contain a specific provision expressly authorising board meetings by electronic means such as video conference.

The legal framework was amended later in 2021. The Emergency Decree on Electronic Meetings B.E. 2563 (2020) was enacted to facilitate electronic meetings during the COVID-19 pandemic, and subsequent amendments to the Civil and Commercial Code (which came into effect in late 2021) introduced Section 1175/1, which now expressly permits board meetings to be held by electronic means if the articles of association allow or the board resolves to do so, provided that the system ensures proper participation and confidentiality.

Therefore, in May 2021, companies conducting electronic board meetings were primarily relying on the Emergency Decree rather than an explicit provision in the Civil and Commercial Code itself.
